one_month_reasoning: Q3 2026 results are expected 2026-11-05 after the close (source 15), i.e. AFTER the 2026-11-01 window, so no company earnings print falls inside it. Events inside the window: (1) hyperscaler Q3 earnings and capex commentary in the last week of October (Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet, Amazon typically report ~Oct 27-30); AAOI's top three customers are 92% of revenue and the stock fell sharply on a Meta CEO remark earlier this year, so this is a two-sided jump risk; (2) continuing sales under the $600M ATM filed 2026-08-21 (source 3), a steady supply overhang that leans slightly negative; (3) recurring 10b5-1 insider sales (source 4), minor. Short interest ~15% of float (source 15) adds squeeze risk on good news. With no scheduled company catalyst I stay close to a symmetric lognormal at monthly vol ~0.38 (139%/3.5 rounded down slightly), with a small negative drift (median ~$114 vs $115.59) for the ATM overhang.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (haircut 2027 EPS $3.50 x 25x = $87.5) and EV/EBITDA (2027 EBITDA ~$528M x 18x + ~$0.3B net cash over ~100M fully diluted shares = $98), 50/50 -> ~$93. Both multiples sit inside but in the lower half of the 12-peer range because of lower gross margin, extreme customer concentration, negative FCF and serial dilution.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2027 non-GAAP EPS $3.50 (consensus $4.60-$5.73 haircut ~25-35%) x 25x forward P/E (peer median 36.7x, range 17-62x)

inputs_detail.derivation: Revenue $2.4B (low end of consensus range $2.40-$3.22B, source 16) x ~14.5% non-GAAP net margin (Q3 guide implies 4-8% net margin on $255-290M at 29-30.5% GM, source 1; margin expands with scale but GM has stayed ~30% for 5 quarters) = ~$350M over ~100M fully diluted shares (84.6M basic at 2026-08-03 per source 8, + ~5M from $600M ATM at ~$120, + ~6M treasury-method Amazon warrant 7.95M @ $23.70 per source 2, + ~2.9M from 2030 Notes per source 2, + RSUs).

Peer median 36.7x (source 17). 25x is near the peer lower quartile (CLS 24.9x, FN 25.5x): AAOI's ~30% GM (source 1) is the contract-manufacturer tier, not the LITE/COHR component tier; top three customers 92% of revenue and $211M of $314M receivables from one distributor (source 2); TTM FCF about -$900M and $1B+ of equity raised in 2026 (sources 2, 9, 15). These are structural and persist through the horizon, so a discount to the median rather than a premium is warranted.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2027 EBITDA ~$528M (revenue $2.4B x 22%) x 18x + net cash ~$0.3B, / ~100M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Low end of consensus range (source 16); Q3 2026 guide $255-290M run-rate ~$1.1B (source 1) must more than double, which requires the 650k units/month capacity target to be met and filled.
Non-GAAP GM ~30% (source 1) less opex ~12% of sales at scale, plus D&A ~4-5% of sales as the >$600M of 2026 capex and prepayments (source 2) start depreciating.

Peer forward EV/EBITDA (proxy: trailing EV/EBITDA x forward P/E / trailing P/E) median ~21x, range 7.5-75x (source 17); 18x sits between CLS (18x) and FN (21x), the closest margin-profile peers, for the same structural reasons as the P/E discount.

$508.8M cash less ~$186M convertible + current debt at 2026-06-30 (source 1), plus remaining ATM proceeds (source 3), less continued heavy capex (H1 2026 capex $335M + $290M prepayments, source 2) and new lease/property commitments (sources 5-7).
84.6M basic (source 8); Q3 guide already uses 92.8M diluted (source 1); add further ATM issuance (source 3).

bear.story: Optical ordering digests in 2027 (as in AAOI's 2018-19 bust) or AAOI loses share at 1.6T to Innolight/Eoptolink/COHR; one of the three customers that make up 92% of revenue cuts orders; GM stays <30% while new Houston/Ningbo capacity sits underused; cash burn forces another equity raise near the lows. 2027 EPS ~$1.5-2 at ~25x.

base.story: Ramp happens but behind consensus: 2027 revenue ~$2.2-2.6B, EPS ~$3.5, share count ~100M; the multiple compresses toward the low-margin hardware peers (~25x on 2027, ~20x on 2028 EPS ~$5).

bull.story: Capacity of 650k units/month is filled at stable ASPs, 2027 revenue >$3B, GM moves into the mid-30s and 2028 EPS ~$8 earns a ~25x multiple; the Amazon relationship broadens.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 17.2x (JBL) to 62.4x (ALAB); forward EV/EBITDA (proxy) 7.5x (JBL) to 75.5x (ALAB). The closest pure-play competitors, Innolight and Eoptolink (Shenzhen-listed), were not included because I could not source their forward multiples in the time available.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 25x 2027 P/E and 18x EV/EBITDA: inside the range, about a 30% and 15% discount to the medians, near CLS/FN.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: A discount that should last through the horizon: (a) gross margin ~30% vs 40%+ at LITE/COHR (source 1); (b) top three customers 92% of Q2 revenue, top ten 99%, and $211M of $314M receivables owed by one CATV distributor (source 2); (c) structurally negative FCF (TTM about -$900M) funded by $1B+ of 2026 equity plus a new $600M ATM, i.e. a falling per-share claim (sources 2, 3, 9, 15); (d) a history of boom-bust cycles and of guidance misses (Q1 2026 miss). No premium is argued.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$62 (about 18x my $3.50 2027 EPS, or EV ~$6B), the market would be pricing 2027 EPS near $2 or less: most likely a lost or cut hyperscaler program (top-3 concentration), a 1.6T qualification failure, or a funding squeeze needing a deeply dilutive raise. That would mean the ramp thesis itself has failed, not ordinary volatility, even with 139% realized vol.

reasoning: Skeptic lane. Primary-filing work: (1) Dilution is the main per-share drag. Basic shares rose from 62.4M (Aug 2025) to 84.6M (Aug 2026, source 8); $1.03B of net equity proceeds came in H1 2026 (source 2), and a further $600M ATM was filed on 2026-08-21 (source 3), which knocked the stock 10-12% (sources 9, 10). The Amazon warrant (7.95M shares at $23.70) and 2030 converts (~2.9M shares) add more (source 2). (2) Cash burn: H1 2026 operating cash flow was -$74M with capex of $335M plus $290M of equipment prepayments; TTM FCF is about -$900M (sources 2, 15). New 10-year leases in Houston and Ningbo and a $26.8M property purchase in September (sources 5-7) lock in fixed costs before demand is proven. (3) Concentration: top 10 = 99% and top 3 = 92% of Q2 revenue; $211M of $314M receivables is owed by Digicomm (source 2). (4) Margins: non-GAAP GM has stuck at ~29-30% and is guided at 29-30.5% for Q3 (source 1); Q1 2026 missed on revenue and EPS. (5) Insiders: parsed Form 4s show ~$94M of sales since April 2026 (mostly 10b5-1 sales and sell-to-cover after large May performance awards), across the CEO, CFO and other officers, and no open-market buys (source 4). That is not a fraud signal, but it is not supportive. (6) Short interest is ~15% of float (source 15). B. Riley's Sell (Nov 2025, $15 PT, source 12) has been wrong so far, and no current short-seller report was found. Weighing it honestly: the demand evidence is real (Q2 revenue +86% y/y, Q3 guided +33-51% q/q, management sees demand above capacity through mid-2027, source 1), and consensus sees 2027 EPS of $4.60-5.73 (sources 14, 16). My fair value of ~$93 haircuts 2027 EPS to $3.50 for dilution and execution and applies lower-half peer multiples (12-peer median fwd P/E 36.7x, source 17). Scenarios: bear $45 (30%), base $105 (45%), bull $200 (25%), probability-weighted mean ~$111. The ladder is a mixture of lognormals (sigma 0.55 bear, 0.35 base/bull), giving a median ~$102, slightly below spot. The tails stay fat, consistent with 139% realized vol and a 52-week range of $18.50-$233.67. Research limits: Alpha Vantage was rate-limited and Twelve Data estimates/targets were paywalled; the consensus figures come from free aggregators dated Aug 2026; X/Twitter and Substack were not searched for speed.
